newsitem.title: CZECH REPUBLIC: Czech leader Havel released from hospital.
newsitem.headline: Czech leader Havel released from hospital.

text.p: Czech President Vaclav Havel was released from hospital on Friday after lung cancer surgery earlier this month, his spokesman said.
Spokesman Ladislav Spacek told Reuters Havel, who had half of his right lung carrying a small malignant tumour removed on December 2, would convalesce at his villa in western Prague.
Havel had been fighting complications from the surgery, and had been on a respirator until late late last week.
Spacek said Havel, 60, tentatively planned to give his traditional New Year address to the nation next Wednesday.
But the speech was expected to be shorter than the president's usual deep monologues about the state of morality and democratic development.
His doctors have said the cancerous tumour was detected at an early stage and there was no sign of the disease spreading.
Pneumonia developed in the opposite lung after the surgery and caused a high fever, but both the pneumonia and the fever have subsided.
Havel, the chain-smoking dissident playwright who helped lead Prague's 1989 bloodless revolution over communism, entered hospital on November 25.
He has not relinquished any constitutional powers, although his office tends to be more ceremonial than executive.
